original_question: On which chromosome is the gene located that is mutated in the disease for which alglucerase was the first FDA-approved enzyme replacement therapy?

final_qi.question: On which chromosome is the gene located that is mutated in the disease for which alglucerase was the first FDA-approved enzyme replacement therapy?
final_qi.long_answer: Alglucerase (Ceredase) was the first FDA-approved enzyme replacement therapy, used for Gaucher disease. Gaucher disease results from mutations in the GBA gene that encodes the lysosomal enzyme β-glucocerebrosidase. The GBA gene is located on chromosome 1 at band 1q21, so the pathogenic mutations reside on chromosome 1.
